question.en:
Consider the following statements about Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park.

I. It lies in Panchmahal district of Gujarat.

II. It was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2014, along with Rani-ki-Vav.

III. It preserves the pre-Mughal capital built by Sultan Mahmud Begada.

Which of the above statements are correct?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 2 — I and III only

Champaner-Pavagadh, in Panchmahal district, Gujarat, was inscribed by UNESCO in 2004, not 2014, and was the first World Heritage Site in Gujarat. Rani-ki-Vav at Patan was inscribed ten years later, in 2014.

The park preserves the Gujarat Sultanate capital that Sultan Mahmud Begada built after taking Pavagadh in 1484 — described by UNESCO as the only complete and unchanged pre-Mughal Islamic city.

Revision note — UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India

  • India has 45 World Heritage Sites — 37 cultural, 7 natural and 1 mixed (Khangchendzonga National Park).
  • Gujarat's four: Champaner-Pavagadh (2004), Rani-ki-Vav, Patan (2014), the Historic City of Ahmedabad (2017) — India's first World Heritage City — and Dholavira (2021).
  • India's first inscriptions, in 1983, were Ajanta, Ellora, the Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal.
  • Maharashtra holds the largest number of sites; the Maratha Military Landscapes were added in 2025.
  • The Kalika Mata temple on Pavagadh hill, a Shakti Peetha, is a living shrine inside the property.
  • The Jama Masjid of Champaner and the Kevada and Nagina mosques blend Hindu and Islamic design.
  • Natural sites include Kaziranga, Manas, Keoladeo, the Sundarbans, Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers, the Great Himalayan National Park and the Western Ghats.
  • Sites are inscribed by the World Heritage Committee under the 1972 Convention; UNESCO is headquartered in Paris.

Gujarat site

Year inscribed

Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park

Rani-ki-Vav, Patan

Do not mix these up

  • Champaner-Pavagadh (2004) was Gujarat's first site; Rani-ki-Vav (2014) is the stepwell at Patan, a decade later.

Also asked from this topic: which UNESCO World Heritage Site is located in Gujarat (SSC MTS 2025), the state in which the Mahabodhi Temple stands (SSC CHSL Tier-1 2025), and the state with the highest number of UNESCO World Heritage Sites (RRB NTPC UG CBT-1 2025-26).

question.en:
Consider the following statements about Carnatic music.

I. Its rhythmic system rests on seven basic talas, the suladi sapta talas.

II. It arranges its ragas under ten parent scales called thaats.

III. The mridangam is its principal percussion accompaniment.

Which of the statements given above are correct?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 1 — I and III only

Carnatic music groups its ragas under 72 melakarta (parent) ragas, a scheme worked out by Venkatamakhin. The ten thaats belong to Hindustani music, as classified by V. N. Bhatkhande — so statement II swaps the two traditions.

The suladi sapta talas — Dhruva, Matya, Rupaka, Jhampa, Triputa, Ata and Eka — give the seven basic talas, and the mridangam is the main percussion instrument of a Carnatic concert.

Revision note — Indian classical music

  • The two streams are Hindustani in the north and Carnatic in the south, both built on raga (melody) and tala (rhythm).
  • Hindustani music absorbed strong Turko-Persian influence; Carnatic music stayed closer to the temple and the Natya Shastra tradition.
  • Carnatic: 72 melakarta ragas; the trinity is Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri; Purandara Dasa is called the Pitamaha of Carnatic music.
  • Carnatic forms: varnam (the concert opener), kriti and ragam-tanam-pallavi; its melodic improvisation is the alapana.
  • Hindustani: ten thaats; forms are dhrupad, khayal, thumri, tappa and tarana; its improvisation is the alap.
  • Hindustani gharanas: Gwalior (the oldest), Kirana, Jaipur-Atrauli, Agra and Patiala; Bettiah and Darbhanga are Dhrupad traditions of Bihar.
  • V. N. Bhatkhande and V. D. Paluskar systematised Hindustani music in the modern period.
  • Carnatic instruments: mridangam, ghatam, kanjira, morsing and the violin; Hindustani uses the tabla, pakhawaj, sarangi and sitar.

question.en:
Consider the following statements about the National Green Hydrogen Mission.

I. Its outlay to 2029-30 is 19,744 crore rupees, most of it for SIGHT.

II. It targets 5 million tonnes of green hydrogen production capacity a year by 2030.

III. It is implemented by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

Which of the above statements are correct?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 4 — I and II only

The Mission, approved in January 2023, has an outlay of 19,744 crore rupees up to 2029-30, of which 17,490 crore rupees goes to SIGHT (Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition), 1,466 crore to pilot projects and 400 crore to research.

It aims at 5 million tonnes a year of green hydrogen capacity by 2030. The nodal ministry is the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, not Petroleum and Natural Gas — which is what makes statement III wrong.

Revision note — National Green Hydrogen Mission

  • Approved by the Union Cabinet in January 2023; implemented by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE).
  • Outlay 19,744 crore rupees to 2029-30: SIGHT 17,490 crore, pilot projects 1,466 crore, research and development 400 crore, other components 388 crore.
  • Targets for 2030: 5 MMT of annual production capacity, about 125 GW of added renewable capacity, over 8 lakh crore rupees of investment and nearly 6 lakh jobs.
  • It also expects to avoid about 1 lakh crore rupees of fossil fuel imports and some 50 MMT of annual carbon dioxide emissions.
  • SIGHT runs two incentive tracks — electrolyser manufacturing and green hydrogen production.
  • The Mission provides for Green Hydrogen Hubs, regions of concentrated production and use, with at least two to be set up by 2030.
  • India's Green Hydrogen Standard caps well-to-gate emissions at 2 kg of CO2 equivalent per kg of hydrogen.
  • Related national targets: 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030 and net zero by 2070, pledged as Panchamrit at COP26, Glasgow.

Type of hydrogen

Do not mix these up

  • Green hydrogen is MNRE's mission; the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas handles ethanol blending and city gas, not this mission.

Also asked from this topic: the production capacity target in million tonnes under the National Green Hydrogen Mission (SSC MTS 2025), the year by which that 5 MMT target is to be met (SSC MTS 2025), and the statement-based question on the aims of the Green Hydrogen Mission (SSC CGL Tier-1 2025).

option_1.en: Races up to and including 400 metres are run in separate lanes

option_2.en: The 1500 metres covers three and three-quarter laps of a 400-metre track

option_3.en: The 800 metres is run in separate lanes from start to finish

option_4.en: The 5000 metres and the 10000 metres are classed as long-distance events

question.en: Which one of the following statements about track events in athletics is NOT correct?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 3 — The 800 metres is run in separate lanes from start to finish

The 800 metres starts in staggered lanes but runners break for the inside lane after the first bend, at the break line. Only races up to and including 400 metres are run entirely in lanes.

The 1500 metres is three and three-quarter laps of a 400-metre track, and the 5000 and 10000 metres are long-distance events run from a mass start.

Revision note — track and field events

  • Sprints: 100 m, 200 m and 400 m, run in lanes from starting blocks; middle distance: 800 m and 1500 m; long distance: 3000 m and above.
  • Laps of a 400-metre track: 800 m = 2, 1500 m = 3 3/4, 5000 m = 12 1/2, 10000 m = 25.
  • A standard outdoor track has eight lanes, each 1.22 m wide, with the inner lane measuring 400 m.
  • The marathon is 42.195 km. From 2026, the senior World Athletics championship race walks use half-marathon (21.0975 km) and marathon (42.195 km) distances, replacing 20 km and 35 km.
  • Hurdle events: 110 m for men and 100 m for women, each with 10 hurdles; the 400 m hurdles also has 10.
  • The 3000 m steeplechase has 28 hurdle jumps and 7 water jumps.
  • In the 4 x 100 m relay the baton must change hands inside a 30-metre takeover zone; the separate acceleration zone was abolished in 2018.
  • The world body is World Athletics, renamed from the IAAF in 2019, with headquarters at Monaco; India's is the Athletics Federation of India.

Do not mix these up

  • Lanes are held for the whole race only up to 400 m; the 800 m breaks after one bend, and from 1500 m upward there is a mass start.

option_1.en: A pawn reaching the eighth rank may become a queen, rook, bishop or knight

option_2.en: Castling is barred if the rook passes a square attacked by the opponent

option_3.en: En passant may be played only on the move after the two-square advance

option_4.en: A stalemate ends the game in a draw however much material a side holds

question.en: Which one of the following statements about the rules of chess is NOT correct?

solution_text.en:
Answer: Option 2 — Castling is barred if the rook passes a square attacked by the opponent

Under the FIDE Laws of Chess the restriction applies to the king, not the rook: castling is illegal if the king is in check, or if it passes over or lands on an attacked square.

The rook may itself be attacked and may cross an attacked square — which is exactly why long castling (0-0-0) stays legal when only the b-file square is covered. Castling is lost for good once the king or that rook has moved.

Revision note — rules of chess

  • The board has 64 squares in an 8 x 8 grid and each side begins with 16 pieces; the corner square at White's right must be light.
  • Promotion: a pawn reaching the far rank must become a queen, rook, bishop or knight — never a king or a pawn — and a second queen is allowed.
  • En passant: a pawn that advances two squares may be taken by an enemy pawn standing on its fifth rank, but only on the very next move.
  • Castling: the king moves two squares towards a rook and the rook jumps to the far side; both must be unmoved and the squares between them empty.
  • Stalemate — no legal move with the king not in check — is a draw, whatever the material.
  • Other draws: threefold repetition, the fifty-move rule, insufficient material and mutual agreement.
  • FIDE, the Federation Internationale des Echecs, was founded in 1924 at Paris and governs world chess; the Chess Olympiad is its team event, held at Chennai in 2022 and Budapest in 2024.
  • Viswanathan Anand became India's first Grandmaster in 1988 and a five-time world champion; D. Gukesh became the youngest undisputed World Chess Champion in 2024.

Term

Meaning

Checkmate

The king is in check with no legal escape — the game is lost

Stalemate

No legal move and the king is not in check — a draw

En passant

A pawn captured 'in passing' after its two-square advance

Castling

The king's two-square move with a rook, allowed once

Do not mix these up

  • In castling the king may not stand in, pass through or land on check; the rook faces no such bar.

Also asked from this topic: what is true about en passant in chess (SSC CGL Tier-1 2025), the term for the move in which a player moves the king and a rook together (SSC Selection Post 2025 (Phase XIII)), and what FIDE stands for (SSC GD 2026).
